pr_title: c2c: write all span config updates from intial scan in one transaction
pr_body:
Previously, the spanConfigIngestor treated updates from the rangefeed initial scan the same way as regular updates: the ingestor would incrementally update the destination side span config table by flushing updates with same source side transaction timestamp. To undestand why this is problematic, recall that an initial scan contains all the latest span config records for the relevant tenant. So, some of these updates may have already been written to the destination side. Further, the initial scan does not replicate source side span config updates that have since been written over by later updates. To summarize, its not possible to replicate a consistent view of the span config table by writing incremental updates surfaced by the initial scan.

In this patch, the ingestor now buffers all updates surfaced by the initial scan and flushes these updates in one transaction which also deletes all existing span config records for the replicating tenant.

Fixes #106823

Release note: None
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/110048)

issue_context.title: c2c: replicate system tenant span configurations
issue_context.body:
To obey a replicating app tenant's zone configurations on the destination cluster, we need to replicate the system tenant's span configuration table, as outlined in section two of this d[esign doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/19BqeHAoCBU24-JFjQY9SGvl_zYt3rLL0jLgVcVbxiZc/edit).  This project has a few steps:

Producer Side
- [x] Refactor the event stream to decode span config kv updates into span config records and send over updates relevant to the replicating tenant

Destination Side
- [x] Within the ingestion job, spin up the span config client for replicating the system tenant span config updates
- [x] Write these span config records to the _online_ system span config table. 
- [x] Buffer up all initial scan keys on resume and write them transactionally

Jira issue: CRDB-29731

review_comments: The initial scan should be relatively rare, so I think it might be a good idea to log something like "flushing initial span configuration state (%d records)"

I wonder if in some sense it would simplify the code.  Namely, I'm thinking we could:

1) Put a bool on the span config event we send over the replication stream indicating it is a full update.
2) In the producer, when we get a full update, flush (or abandon) whatever is in our current buffer and then send the full update.
3) In the consumer, when we get a full update, flush (or abandon) whatever is in our current buffer and then flushInitialScan on the new data.

In this way, we also wouldn't have any state consumer-side about whether or not the initial scan was complete. I could see this being a useful architecture even if we didn't move to using rangefeedcache.Start().

That said, this is just food for thought.  Not an essential change.

hrm. i could go either way. One thing to note is that the initial scan buffer always flushes on checkpoint receipt. For your consumer side stateless proposal to hold, we'd need to add a `spanConfigInitialScanComplete` field to the [checkpointEvent struct](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/f716fc187522654908f1bd71880d5cd9e9e70be4/pkg/ccl/streamingccl/event.go#L177) or create a new kind of checkpointEvent for spanConfig updates. I guess there are trade offs to every thing 🤷 . 

Let's merge what I have now and continue to stew? We may need to implement the internal retry stuff anyway.

Agree.

a retort that doesn't matter at all: isn't it safer to use the builder's public api to add state to it?

:D fmt.Fprintf takes a Writer and strings.Builder is a Writer per its public API: https://pkg.go.dev/strings#Builder.Write

Anyway, don't change this. Next time I'll not let the intrusive thoughts convince me to write this comment.

This modification inside the transaction is OK because we aren't also reading from it inside the transaction. We could potentially prevent future misuse by only modifying this after the transaction has returned.
I assume we are guaranteed that a CompleteUpdate will always have had at least one span configuration record?
Right, we expect that the initial scan of the tenant's span config table will _always_ have something in it. If not, something is very wrong.
